earlier_scan.source_named: Fricke, Hanna L.A. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages. PhD diss., Leiden (West Lembata material pp. 171-228 per Glottolog).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record west2541 (West Lembata): dialects Labalekan [Imulolo, Lewopenutu, Lewotala], Mingar; Glottolog's most extensive description = Keraf 1978 'a wordlist or less'.
sources.note: n/a — confirms the only reference is a wordlist.

sources.citation: Lamak, Maria Lambertina Beto, Simon Sabon Ola & Anastasia J. M. Leda. 2026. Makna dan nilai tuturan Popas Lata pasca nikahan pada etnik Lamaholot di Desa Puor Pulau Lembata [Meanings and values of post-wedding Popas Lata utterances among the Lamaholot of Puor village, Lembata]. YASIN: Jurnal Pendidikan dan Sosial Budaya 6(5): 6116-6130. Universitas Nusa Cendana authors. DOI 10.58578/yasin.v6i5.11471.
sources.note: no phonology content: linguistic-anthropology description of the Popas Lata (hair-washing) post-wedding ritual, its social meanings, values and stages, written in Indonesian with a handful of Lamaholot ritual terms (Koda Klaken, Titen Ballen, welin ela, Jedo Pare Tonu Wujo, Pao-Hula); no transcription conventions, no remarks on sounds, stress, accent or intonation (a full-text search for stress/accent tekanan/aksen/fonologi/fonem/bunyi/intonasi/prosodi/nada/suku kata: nothing).
sources.venue: YASIN: Jurnal Pendidikan dan Sosial Budaya

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2025 [PDF dated 2026]. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press. 620+ pp. (Glottolog ref 710158; langsci catalog/book/526; Zenodo record 18323007.)
sources.note: No statement about lmj prosody. lmj appears only in sound-correspondence tables (Mingar nusa/saur; Labalekan baha/haur, pana/ləʤaf/mataʤ), in the note that Mingar retains *s = s in some words, and in the subgrouping tree (**v > f). The only stress content nearby is areal (sec. 3.2.1, on schwa in languages of Flores): 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables' — a generalisation over the region, not a description of West Lembata, so not entered as a statement.

sources.citation: Nugroho, Zefanya Christiady & Heppy Christinawati Silaen. 2024. Dinamika ketahanan bahasa-bahasa rumpun Lamaholot di Lembata. Linguistik Indonesia 42(1): 221-245. DOI 10.26499/li.v42i1.578.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content — Wheel of Vitality / Mountain Metaphor results; West Lembata rated EGIDS 7 (shifting) at Bour; the only 'tekanan' in the text means social 'pressure'.

sources.citation: Swalar, Thomas Krispianus. 2024. Deiksis persona bahasa Lamaholot dialek Lamaholot Tengah. MAJU: Indonesian Journal of Community Empowerment 1(3): 83-93. DOI 10.62335/t792n796.
sources.note: no phonology content — person-deixis forms and c. 20 glossed example dialogues in plain orthography; no mention of tekanan/aksen/fonologi.
sources.venue: MAJU: Indonesian Journal of Community Empowerment

sources.citation: Bala, Alexander [= Alexander Bala Gawen, Universitas Flores]. 2022. Membedah nilai ketuhanan dan kemanusiaan dalam nyanyian "Oreng" pada etnik Lamaholot di Imulolong. Arif: Jurnal Sastra dan Kearifan Lokal 2(1). DOI 10.21009/arif.021.04.
sources.note: no phonology content — hermeneutic/ethnolinguistic reading of oreng song lines (lmj text fragments with Indonesian glosses); no remarks on sound system, stress or intonation.

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna L. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages in eastern Indonesia. PhD dissertation, Leiden University (LOT 544). Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Nothing for lmj. Table of varieties (pp.161-162) lists Imulolo, Lewopenutu, Lewotala, Mingar (ISO lmj) with sole source 'Keraf 1978b' (200-item wordlists); p.159: 'Central Lamaholot has been largely undescribed. Until recently, the 200 items wordlists of eight Central Lamaholot varieties in Keraf (1978a) were the only published information on Central Lamaholot.' The stress section (3.2.5, p.49) is for Central Lembata (lvu, levu1239) only: penultimate stress unless the penult is schwa, then final.

sources.citation: Kaiping, Gereon A., Owen Edwards & Marian Klamer (eds.). 2019-. LexiRumah 3.0.0 lexical database: lects lama1277-imulo 'Labalekan, Imulolo', lama1277-lewop 'Labalekan, Lewopenutu', lama1277-lewot 'Labalekan, Lewotala', lama1277-minga 'Mingar' (all ISO lmj; source keraf1978). Leiden University Centre for Linguistics.
sources.note: wordlist-only data: 799 segmental transcriptions (e.g. Imulolo kələm 'sky', ləd͡ʒaf 'sun', faer 'water'); no stress or tone marks in Form or Segments columns (Keraf's é/e distinguish /e/ from schwa, not accent). Not a statement.

sources.citation: Michels, Marc. 2017. Western Lamaholot: A cross-dialectal grammar sketch. MA thesis, Leiden.
sources.note: Nothing for lmj (Western Lamaholot only). Confirms 'Keraf focused his morphological description solely on the dialect spoken in Lamalera' and otherwise gives only a 33-dialect Swadesh-list lexicostatistics.

sources.citation: Krausse, Daniel. 2016. A brief grammatical sketch of Eastern Atadei (Atadei Painara), Lembata. (paper/MA-level sketch)
sources.note: Nothing for lmj; describes Eastern Atadei (lmf, sout2896). Cites Keraf 1978 pp.409-423 only for wordlist forms of Lewotala, Imulolo, Mingar, Lewopenutu; states Keraf's dissertation covers the West Lembata dialects only in its lexicostatistical survey.

sources.citation: Nagaya, Naonori. 2012. The Lamaholot language of eastern Flores, Indonesia. PhD dissertation, Rice University.
sources.note: Nothing for lmj (Lewotobi, WL). Notes Keraf 1978 offers only Swadesh 200 lists for the other dialects.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa (Kemendikdasmen). n.d. [c. 2008-2019 mapping]. Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Lamaholot, Provinsi Nusa Tenggara Timur' (language-mapping database entry: 17 dialectometric dialects over 23 observation points, incl. dialek Pasir Putih and dialek Watobuku (Naga Wutung), Lembata) and companion entry 'Bahasa Kalela (Kawela)' (idb=250: Katakeja/Kalikasa, Lerek, Boto-Labalimut). Jakarta: Badan Bahasa.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing: the entry gives villages, the statement that Lamaholot differs >81% (dialectometry) from Kawela, Hewa, Kedang and Sikka, and the list of 17 dialects/subdialects by observation point; no phonology, no stress or tone remark. Useful only as the official Indonesian mapping pointer (the underlying Balai/Kantor Bahasa NTT survey volumes with the 23 wordlists are not linked).

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E., Tom Therik, Barbara Dix Grimes & Max Jacob. 1997. A guide to the people and languages of Nusa Tenggara. (Paradigma B-1.) Kupang: Artha Wacana Press. Entry 'LEMBATA, WEST' pp.82-83.
sources.note: Nothing. The West Lembata entry (the text) gives alternate names, classification (Austronesian, CMP, Timor, Flores-Lembata), location, 'Number in ethnic group: unknown', 'Comments: Lamaholot is used as a language of wider communication'. No phonology anywhere in the Lembata entries; a full-text search for stress/accent over the whole guide text returns no linguistic hit.

sources.citation: Akoli, Marcelinus Y. F. 2010. [MA thesis on the Lewokukung variety of Lamaholot, Lembata] (cited in Fricke 2019:159 as describing 'aspects of the Lewokukung variety, based on a wordlist of 200 basic items and a transcribed and translated folk story').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Nearest additional Central Lamaholot description; Lewokukung is classed by Fricke under Levuka (lvu) but is geographically adjacent to the Labalekan/Mingar lects; would only be a proxy, not an lmj source.

sources.citation: Keraf, Gregorius. 1978. Morfologi Dialek Lamalera. Doctoral dissertation, Universitas Indonesia, Jakarta (esp. wordlists pp.262-297 / 'Daftar Kata Dasar' pp.406-447 for Imulolo, Lewopenutu, Lewotala, Mingar).

sources.note: The only primary publication with any lmj data (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description). Its descriptive chapters treat Lamalera (lmr) only, but the transcribed wordlists might carry accent marks and the introduction may contain a general remark on stress across the 33 surveyed Lamaholot dialects; worth checking if a scan can be obtained.
